historical_conflict_sector_impact:
| Conflict Event | Period | Defense Sector | Energy (Oil) | Financial/Banking | Safe Haven/Other |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gulf War** | 1990-1991 | Outperformed S&P 500 (Lockheed, Raytheon) | Oil $15 → $40 (Peak Volatility) | Saudi banks saw 11% deposit outflow; high recession fears | Gold peaked >$400/oz then corrected |
| **Iraq War** | 2003 | Tailwinds during build-up; broad rally after invasion | Fluctuated with supply fears; sharp rally post-invasion | Stabilized after initial uncertainty-driven 5.6% S&P drop | DJIA +8.4% in one month post-invasion |
| **Soleimani Strike** | 2020 | Moderate performance; Cyber security emerged as new hedge | Transient price spikes; recovered within 72 hours | Minimal sustained disruption | Gold/Treasuries saw 15-20% inflows; safe haven status solidified |
| **Gaza/Iran Crisis** | 2023-2024 | Sustained outperformance amid regional proxy wars | WTI peaked ~$87-90/bbl; supply cycle driven | High rate sensitivity; focus on risk premium expansion | Gold (GLD) hit record ~$2,400; superior to US 10Y Treasuries |

Key patterns identified across historical data: 1) Initial uncertainty leads to a 2-8% outperformance in defense and energy sectors. 2) Actual military engagement often triggers a 'buy the news' rally in broader markets as uncertainty resolves. 3) Financial sectors in the immediate conflict zone (e.g., Middle East banks) face significant liquidity risks, while global finance reacts to recession/inflation cues. 4) The 2020/2024 periods show a shift where Cyber Security stocks and Gold have become more effective hedges than traditional Treasuries due to high interest rate environments.

result.oct_nov_2023_analysis: Between Oct 6 and Nov 7, 2023, the S&P 500 initially dropped 2.12% but rebounded 8.72% by late November as the conflict remained localized. Gold (GLD) saw safe-haven inflows of $8.2 billion, while WTI Crude Oil peaked near $90/bbl before retreating. US 10Y Treasury yields remained volatile, influenced by both safe-haven bids and inflation concerns.
result.apr_may_2024_analysis: During the April 12 to May 13, 2024 Iran-Israel escalation, the S&P 500 declined 4.23%. Gold hit a record high near $2,400, and WTI Oil reached $87/bbl. US 10Y Treasury yields climbed toward 4.7% as risk premiums expanded and inflation expectations shifted.

| US 10Y Yield | Fluctuating | Peak 4.7% | Risk premium expansion |

result.volatility_pattern: Both periods exhibited a 'front-loaded' volatility profile where markets reacted sharply within the first 10-14 days of escalation. Stabilization occurred rapidly once it became clear that energy supply chains (Strait of Hormuz) were not directly severed.

result.etf_flow_analysis: During the escalation of Middle East conflicts (Oct 2023, Apr 2024), safe-haven demand was dominant but bifurcated. Gold ETFs (GLD) saw massive inflows, peaking with global net inflows of $8.2bn in Oct 2023 and strong momentum in 2024 (+$26bn in Q3). Fixed Income (TLT) experienced high volatility with initial inflows followed by $6bn outflows as inflation/interest rate concerns weighed. Risk-off patterns were evidenced by SPY volatility and UUP (USD) acting as a relative stability anchor, though specific UUP flow data was less pronounced than the surge in Gold.
risk_off_patterns: Gold (GLD/GLDM) remains the primary hedge during Iran-linked escalations.
Fixed Income (TLT) flows are currently compromised by 'higher-for-longer' interest rate narratives, reducing its efficacy as a pure geopolitical hedge compared to historical norms.
USD (UUP) maintains a positive correlation with conflict escalation as a liquidity proxy.
